docs.title: faststream-gcp-pubsub
docs.text:
A Google Cloud Pub/Sub broker for FastStream, maintained by the community.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream
from pydantic import BaseModel

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSub, PubSubBroker


class Order(BaseModel):
    id: int
    amount: float


broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)

shipments = broker.publisher("shipments")


@broker.subscriber(PubSub("orders-billing"), topic="orders")
@shipments
async def bill(order: Order) -> dict[str, int]:
    # the return value is published to the `shipments` topic
    return {"order_id": order.id}


@app.after_startup
async def place_order() -> None:
    await broker.publish(Order(id=1, amount=9.5), "orders")

faststream run service:app

The handler reads the orders-billing subscription of the orders topic, decodes the JSON body into Order, acknowledges the message once the handler returns, and publishes its result to shipments.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pipuv 
pip install faststream-gcp-pubsub

uv add faststream-gcp-pubsub

The package needs Python 3.10 or newer and FastStream 0.7. The extras are otel (OpenTelemetry), prometheus and cli (the faststream command):

pip install "faststream-gcp-pubsub[cli,otel,prometheus]"

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Subscribers read a subscription through a streaming pull and keep each message leased until the handler settles it.
  • Publishers send one message or a batch, with attributes, ordering keys and message ids.
  • Topics, subscriptions, dead-letter and retry policies are created at startup when you declare them.
  • Acknowledgement follows the Pub/Sub model: ack, nack for immediate redelivery, and reject as an acknowledgement.
  • Flow control bounds the messages and bytes held at once; acks travel in batches.
  • TestPubSubBroker runs the service in process, with routing and validation like the real service.
  • The Pub/Sub emulator, Application Default Credentials, service account keys and regional endpoints are supported.
  • FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and AsyncAPI integrations are included.

def __init__(
    self,
    project_id: str = EMPTY,
    *,
    emulator_host: str | None = EMPTY,
    api_endpoint: str | None = None,
    client_options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    graceful_timeout: float | None = 15.0,
    decoder: Optional["CustomCallable"] = None,
    parser: Optional["CustomCallable"] = None,
    codec: Optional["CodecProto"] = None,
    dependencies: Sequence["Dependant"] = (),
    middlewares: Sequence["BrokerMiddleware[Any, Any]"] = (),
    routers: Iterable[PubSubRegistrator] = (),
    ack_policy: AckPolicy = EMPTY,
    id_generator: IdGenerator = gen_cor_id,
    # AsyncAPI args
    specification_url: str | None = None,
    protocol: str | None = None,
    protocol_version: str | None = "v1",
    description: str | None = None,
    tags: Iterable["Tag | TagDict"] = (),
    security: Optional["BaseSecurity"] = None,
    # logging args
    logger: Optional["LoggerProto"] = EMPTY,
    log_level: int = logging.INFO,
    # FastDepends args
    apply_types: bool = True,
    serializer: Optional["SerializerProto"] = EMPTY,
    provider: Optional["Provider"] = None,
    context: Optional["ContextRepo"] = None,
) -> None:
    if project_id is EMPTY:
        project_id = os.environ.get("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT", "")
    if emulator_host is EMPTY:
        emulator_host = os.environ.get("PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST") or None

    self._connection_options = ConnectionOptions(
        emulator_host=emulator_host,
        credentials=parse_security(security),
        api_endpoint=api_endpoint,
        client_options=client_options,
    )

    if specification_url is None:
        specification_url = emulator_host or api_endpoint or DEFAULT_ENDPOINT

    super().__init__(
        # broker config
        routers=routers,
        config=PubSubBrokerConfig(
            project_id=project_id,
            producer=PubSubProducer(parser=parser, decoder=decoder),
            broker_middlewares=middlewares,
            broker_parser=parser,
            broker_decoder=decoder,
            broker_codec=codec,
            logger=make_pubsub_logger_state(
                logger=logger,
                log_level=log_level,
            ),
            fd_config=FastDependsConfig(
                use_fastdepends=apply_types,
                serializer=serializer,
                provider=provider or dependency_provider,
                context=context or ContextRepo(),
            ),
            broker_dependencies=dependencies,
            graceful_timeout=graceful_timeout,
            ack_policy=ack_policy,
            id_generator=id_generator,
            extra_context={
                "broker": self,
            },
        ),
        specification=BrokerSpec(
            description=description,
            url=[specification_url],
            protocol=protocol or "googlepubsub",
            protocol_version=protocol_version,
            tags=tags,
            security=security,
        ),
    )

async def declare_topic(self, topic: str | PubSubTopic) -> str:
    """Create a topic unless it exists.

    Returns:
        The full resource name of the topic.
    """
    topic_ = topic if isinstance(topic, PubSubTopic) else PubSubTopic(topic)
    request = topic_.to_proto(self.config.project_id)
    with contextlib.suppress(AlreadyExists):
        await self.config.connection.publisher.create_topic(request=request)
    return str(request.name)

async def declare_subscription(
    self,
    subscription: str | PubSub,
    topic: str | PubSubTopic,
) -> str:
    """Create a subscription attached to ``topic`` unless it exists; the topic must exist.

    Returns:
        The full resource name of the subscription.
    """
    subscription_ = (
        subscription if isinstance(subscription, PubSub) else PubSub(subscription)
    )
    topic_name = topic.name if isinstance(topic, PubSubTopic) else topic
    project = self.config.project_id
    request = subscription_.to_proto(
        project, resource_path(project, "topics", topic_name)
    )
    with contextlib.suppress(AlreadyExists):
        await self.config.connection.subscriber.create_subscription(request=request)
    return str(request.name)

@override
async def publish(
    self,
    message: "SendableMessage" = None,
    topic: str = "",
    *,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ordering_key: str = "",
    correlation_id: str | None = None,
    reply_to: str = "",
    timeout: float | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Publish a message to a topic.

    Args:
        message: the message body.
        topic: the topic, a short id or a full resource name.
        headers: message attributes.
        ordering_key: messages of one key are delivered in publish order to a subscription
            with message ordering; publish them one after another.
        correlation_id: the correlation id; generated when omitted.
        reply_to: the topic a consumer publishes its reply to.
        timeout: the RPC deadline in seconds; the client's default when omitted.

    Returns:
        The message id the service assigned.
    """
    cmd = PubSubPublishCommand(
        message,
        topic=topic,
        headers=headers,
        ordering_key=ordering_key,
        correlation_id=correlation_id or self.config.id_generator(),
        reply_to=reply_to,
        timeout=timeout,
        _publish_type=PublishType.PUBLISH,
    )
    result: str = await self._basic_publish(cmd, producer=self.config.producer)
    return result

def to_proto(self, project_id: str, topic: str) -> "Subscription":
    """The subscription resource the broker creates, attached to ``topic`` (a full name)."""
    from google.pubsub_v1 import Subscription  # ruff: ignore[import-outside-top-level]

    options: dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": self.path(project_id),
        "topic": topic,
        "enable_message_ordering": self.enable_message_ordering,
        "enable_exactly_once_delivery": self.enable_exactly_once_delivery,
        "filter": self.filter,
        "labels": self.labels,
    }
    if self.ack_deadline_seconds is not None:
        options["ack_deadline_seconds"] = self.ack_deadline_seconds
    if self.message_retention_duration is not None:
        options["message_retention_duration"] = self.message_retention_duration
    if self.dead_letter_policy is not None:
        options["dead_letter_policy"] = {
            "dead_letter_topic": resource_path(
                project_id, "topics", self.dead_letter_policy.topic
            ),
            "max_delivery_attempts": self.dead_letter_policy.max_delivery_attempts,
        }
    if self.retry_policy is not None:
        options["retry_policy"] = {
            "minimum_backoff": self.retry_policy.minimum_backoff,
            "maximum_backoff": self.retry_policy.maximum_backoff,
        }
    return Subscription(**options)

def create_publisher_fake_subscriber(
    self,
    broker: PubSubBroker,
    publisher: "PubSubPublisher",
) -> tuple["PubSubBaseSubscriber", bool]:
    project = broker.config.project_id
    topic = resource_path(project, "topics", publisher.topic)
    for b in self.brokers:
        for s in b.subscribers:
            sub = cast("PubSubBaseSubscriber", s)
            if resource_path(b.config.project_id, "topics", sub.topic) == topic:
                return sub, True

    # Under `with_real` the subscription is created on the service only when the
    # publisher declares its topic: a test never adds resources nobody asked for.
    subscription = PubSub(publisher.topic, declare=publisher.topic_schema.declare)
    sub = cast(
        "PubSubBaseSubscriber", broker.subscriber(subscription, persistent=False)
    )
    return sub, False

docs.title: AsyncAPI
docs.text:
FastStream generates an AsyncAPI document of the service. Subscribers appear with their subscription and topic, publishers with their topic.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(
    project_id="my-project",
    description="Orders of the shop",
)
app = FastStream(broker)

shipments = broker.publisher("shipments", description="Orders ready to ship")


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders", description="Bills an order")
@shipments
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {"order_id": order["id"]}

Serve the document in the browser:

faststream docs serve service:app

Write it to a file:

faststream docs gen service:app

title, description and include_in_schema of subscribers and publishers set the text of the operations. The broker's description, tags, specification_url and protocol set the server entry. The server entry carries the coordinate the broker connects to and never credentials.

docs.title: Consuming
docs.text:
A handler is a function decorated with @broker.subscriber. It receives the decoded body and any FastStream dependencies.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream, Header, Logger

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker, PubSubMessage

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(
    order: dict[str, int],
    msg: PubSubMessage,
    logger: Logger,
    region: str = Header(default="eu"),
) -> None:
    logger.info(
        "order %s from %s: message %s, key %r, published %s",
        order["id"],
        region,
        msg.raw_message.message_id,
        msg.ordering_key,
        msg.raw_message.publish_time,
    )

msg is the PubSubMessage of the delivery. Its ordering_key and delivery_attempt properties and the raw_message (message_id, publish_time, attributes, data) describe what the service sent. Attributes are also available as headers.

docs.title: Acknowledgement
docs.text:
The default policy is AckPolicy.NACK_ON_ERROR: the message is acknowledged when the handler returns and nacked when it raises. Pub/Sub maps the settlements this way:

Settlement What Pub/Sub does ack The message is acknowledged and not delivered again. nack The ack deadline is set to zero and the message is available for redelivery at once. reject The message is acknowledged. Pub/Sub has no reject.

A failed message is redelivered under the subscription's retry policy and moves to its dead-letter topic after the last attempt. That is how a poison message leaves a subscription.

The policy is set per subscriber with ack_policy= or for the broker with PubSubBroker(ack_policy=...).

docs.title: Manual settlement
docs.text:
With AckPolicy.MANUAL the handler settles the message.

service.py
from faststream import AckPolicy, FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker, PubSubMessage

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders", ack_policy=AckPolicy.MANUAL)
async def bill(order: dict[str, int], msg: PubSubMessage) -> None:
    if order["amount"] < 0:
        # Pub/Sub has no reject: the message is acknowledged and dropped
        await msg.reject()
    elif order["amount"] == 0:
        # available for redelivery at once
        await msg.nack()
    else:
        await msg.ack()

docs.title: Delivery attempts
docs.text:
msg.delivery_attempt counts the deliveries of a message. The service fills it when the subscription has a dead-letter policy and the value is 0 otherwise.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream, Logger

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import (
    DeadLetterPolicy,
    PubSub,
    PubSubBroker,
    PubSubMessage,
)

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)

billing = PubSub(
    "orders-billing",
    declare=True,
    dead_letter_policy=DeadLetterPolicy("orders-dead", max_delivery_attempts=5),
)


@broker.subscriber(billing, topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int], msg: PubSubMessage, logger: Logger) -> None:
    # counts deliveries; it is 0 on a subscription without a dead-letter policy
    logger.info("attempt %d of order %s", msg.delivery_attempt, order["id"])
    if msg.delivery_attempt < 3:
        error = "retry later"
        raise ValueError(error)

docs.title: Reading messages without a handler
docs.text:
A subscriber without a handler is read by hand. get_one pulls one message and returns None when none arrives within the timeout.

service.py
from typing import Any

from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)

# a subscriber without a handler is read by hand
orders = broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")


async def read_one() -> Any | None:
    message = await orders.get_one(timeout=5.0)
    if message is None:
        return None
    order = await message.decode()
    await message.ack()
    return order

Iterating the subscriber reads a stream of messages:

service.py
from typing import Any

from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)

orders = broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")


async def read_all() -> list[Any]:
    received: list[Any] = []
    async for message in orders:
        received.append(await message.decode())
        await message.ack()
        if len(received) == 3:
            break
    return received

The messages are settled by hand, as no handler stands behind them.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
By default a subscriber handles one message at a time. max_workers handles that many at once.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


# ten deliveries are handled at once
@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders", max_workers=10)
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

max_workers works together with flow control: the subscriber reads at most max_messages messages that are not settled.

docs.title: Declaring resources
docs.text:
A resource is created when its declaration says declare=True. The broker creates the topic and the subscription at startup if they do not exist.

service.py
from datetime import timedelta

from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import (
    DeadLetterPolicy,
    PubSub,
    PubSubBroker,
    PubSubTopic,
    RetryPolicy,
)

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)

orders = PubSubTopic(
    "orders",
    declare=True,
    labels={"team": "billing"},
    message_retention_duration=timedelta(days=1),
)

billing = PubSub(
    "orders-billing",
    declare=True,
    ack_deadline_seconds=30,
    enable_message_ordering=True,
    enable_exactly_once_delivery=True,
    filter='attributes.region = "eu"',
    dead_letter_policy=DeadLetterPolicy("orders-dead", max_delivery_attempts=5),
    retry_policy=RetryPolicy(
        minimum_backoff=timedelta(seconds=10),
        maximum_backoff=timedelta(seconds=300),
    ),
    message_retention_duration=timedelta(days=2),
    labels={"team": "billing"},
)


@broker.subscriber(billing, topic=orders)
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

An existing resource keeps its own settings: the declaration applies only to a resource the broker creates. The dead-letter topic of the policy is created too.

docs.title: PubSubTopic
docs.text: Field Meaning name A short id or a full resource name. declare Create the topic at startup when it does not exist. labels Labels of a created topic. message_retention_duration How long a created topic keeps messages for seek.

docs.title: PubSub
docs.text: Field Meaning name A short id or a full resource name. declare Create the subscription, and its topic, at startup when they do not exist. ack_deadline_seconds The ack deadline of a created subscription, 10 to 600 seconds. enable_message_ordering Deliver messages of one ordering key in publish order. enable_exactly_once_delivery Let an acknowledged message never be redelivered. See exactly-once delivery. filter A filter expression on attributes. The service acknowledges messages it rejects and delivers none of them. dead_letter_policy A DeadLetterPolicy. retry_policy A RetryPolicy. message_retention_duration How long unacknowledged messages are kept. labels Labels of a created subscription.

docs.title: DeadLetterPolicy
docs.text:
A message that fails too often moves to the dead-letter topic.

Field Meaning topic The dead-letter topic, a short id or a full name. max_delivery_attempts Attempts before the move, 5 to 100. The default is 5.

docs.title: RetryPolicy
docs.text:
A nacked message is redelivered after a backoff.

Field Meaning minimum_backoff The shortest delay, 0 to 600 seconds. The default is 10 seconds. maximum_backoff The longest delay, 0 to 600 seconds. The default is 600 seconds.

docs.title: Declaring by hand
docs.text:
declare_topic and declare_subscription create resources at a point you choose. Both ignore a resource that exists and return the full resource name. The topic of a subscription must exist.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSub, PubSubBroker, PubSubTopic

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@app.after_startup
async def declare() -> None:
    topic = await broker.declare_topic(PubSubTopic("orders", labels={"team": "billing"}))
    subscription = await broker.declare_subscription(
        PubSub("orders-billing", ack_deadline_seconds=30),
        topic="orders",
    )
    # both return the full resource name
    assert topic == "projects/my-project/topics/orders"
    assert subscription == "projects/my-project/subscriptions/orders-billing"

docs.title: The emulator
docs.text:
The broker connects to the Pub/Sub emulator, with no credentials, when the PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST variable is set or emulator_host is passed.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

# also read from PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST when the argument is omitted
broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="faststream-test", emulator_host="localhost:8085")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

emulator_host=None connects to Google Cloud even when the variable is set. The getting started page shows how to start the emulator with the repository's docker-compose.yaml.

docs.title: Project
docs.text: project_id names the project short topic and subscription names belong to. When it is omitted, the broker reads GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Without a security object the broker uses Application Default Credentials: the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS key file, the gcloud login, or the metadata server of Google Cloud. GCPSecurity passes other credentials.

service.py
from google.oauth2 import service_account

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import GCPSecurity, PubSubBroker


def from_key_file() -> PubSubBroker:
    return PubSubBroker(
        project_id="my-project",
        security=GCPSecurity.from_service_account_file("key.json"),
    )


def from_credentials() -> PubSubBroker:
    credentials = service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_file("key.json")
    return PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project", security=GCPSecurity(credentials))

GCPSecurity also has from_service_account_info, which takes the parsed JSON key. Any google.auth credentials object works with GCPSecurity(credentials).

docs.title: Endpoints and client options
docs.text:
api_endpoint selects a regional or private endpoint. client_options passes other google.api_core.client_options to both clients.

service.py
from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(
    project_id="my-project",
    api_endpoint="europe-west1-pubsub.googleapis.com:443",
    client_options={"quota_project_id": "billing-project"},
)

docs.title: FastAPI
docs.text:
PubSubRouter from faststream_gcp_pubsub.fastapi is a FastAPI router that owns a broker. It takes the options of PubSubBroker and of fastapi.APIRouter.

app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI

from faststream_gcp_pubsub.fastapi import PubSubRouter

router = PubSubRouter(project_id="my-project")


@router.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


@router.post("/orders")
async def place_order(order: dict[str, int]) -> str:
    return await router.broker.publish(order, "orders")


app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(router)

Subscribers start with the FastAPI application and stop with it. router.broker is the PubSubBroker, so router.broker.publish(...) publishes from a route.

The broker's dependencies are FastAPI dependencies here, and its tags are specification_tags.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Test the router with the broker it owns:

test_app.py
    async with TestPubSubBroker(router.broker) as br:
        await br.publish({"id": 1}, "orders")

        bill.mock.assert_called_once_with({"id": 1})

The module also exports PubSubMessage, PubSubBroker, Connection, Context, ContextRepo and Logger as FastAPI-aware annotations for handler arguments.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
A service is a PubSubBroker, a FastStream app and handlers.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream, Logger

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def handle(order: dict[str, int], logger: Logger) -> None:
    logger.info("order %s", order["id"])

The handler reads the subscription orders-billing, which is attached to the topic orders. The broker is built without any network call; it connects when the app starts.

docs.title: Run the service
docs.text:
Install the cli extra, then start the app with the faststream command:

pip install "faststream-gcp-pubsub[cli]"
faststream run service:app

The service authenticates with Application Default Credentials. On a workstation, gcloud auth application-default login creates them. Other ways to authenticate are on the Emulator and credentials page.

Pub/Sub keeps topics and subscriptions as separate resources, and a service reads from resources that exist. The next sections create them for local work.

docs.title: Run against the emulator
docs.text:
The repository ships a docker-compose.yaml that starts the Pub/Sub emulator:

docker-compose.yaml
services:
  pubsub:
    image: gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:emulators
    command: gcloud beta emulators pubsub start --host-port=0.0.0.0:8085 --project=faststream-test
    ports:
      - "${PUBSUB_EMULATOR_PORT:-8085}:8085"

The justfile has the recipes you need:

Recipe What it does just emulator-up Starts the emulator on port 8085 (set PUBSUB_EMULATOR_PORT to change it) and waits until it is ready. just test-gcp Runs the tests marked gcp against the emulator. just emulator-down Stops the emulator.

A service connects to the emulator with emulator_host. A subscription declared with declare=True creates its topic and itself at startup, so the emulator needs no setup:

service.py
from faststream import FastStream, Logger

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSub, PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="faststream-test", emulator_host="localhost:8085")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber(PubSub("orders-billing", declare=True), topic="orders")
async def handle(order: dict[str, int], logger: Logger) -> None:
    logger.info("order %s", order["id"])


@app.after_startup
async def place_order() -> None:
    await broker.publish({"id": 1}, "orders")

just emulator-up
faststream run service:app

The handler logs the order that place_order publishes after startup.

Tip

Setting PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:8085 in the environment has the same effect as emulator_host, so the service code stays the same in production.

docs.title: Test the service
docs.text:
TestPubSubBroker runs the handlers in process:

test_service.py
@pytest.mark.asyncio()
async def test_service() -> None:
    async with TestPubSubBroker(broker) as br:
        await br.publish({"id": 1}, "orders")

        handle.mock.assert_called_once_with({"id": 1})

Read Testing for the routing rules of the in-process broker.

docs.title: Leases and flow control
docs.text:
The subscriber reads through a streaming pull and keeps each message leased: it extends the ack deadline of every message in work until the handler settles it, up to max_lease. FlowControl bounds what the subscriber holds at once.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import FlowControl, PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project", graceful_timeout=30.0)
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber(
    "orders-billing",
    topic="orders",
    flow_control=FlowControl(
        max_messages=100,
        max_bytes=10 * 1024 * 1024,
        ack_deadline=60,
        max_lease=1800.0,
        ack_batch_wait=0.05,
    ),
    max_workers=10,
)
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...
Field Default Meaning max_messages 1000 Deliveries held at once, unsettled. The stream is not read further until one settles. At least 1. max_bytes 100 MiB Payload bytes held at once. The service stops sending past it. ack_deadline 60 s The length of a lease before it is extended, 10 to 600. max_lease 3600 s The longest a delivery is held. Past it the lease is no longer extended and the service redelivers the message. ack_batch_wait 0.05 s How long acks and nacks wait to be sent together.

Choose max_lease above the longest time a handler can take. A handler that outlives it loses its message to a redelivery.

docs.title: Batched settlement
docs.text: Acks and nacks of one subscription are sent together: one request per ack_batch_wait, or per 1000 ids, which is the largest request the service takes. The handler does not wait for the request.

docs.title: Exactly-once delivery
docs.text:
On a subscription with enable_exactly_once_delivery=True the service guarantees that an acknowledged message is not delivered again. There ack() waits for the service's confirmation and raises when the service refuses it.

service.py
from faststream import AckPolicy, FastStream, Logger

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSub, PubSubBroker, PubSubMessage

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)

billing = PubSub(
    "orders-billing",
    declare=True,
    enable_exactly_once_delivery=True,
)


@broker.subscriber(billing, topic="orders", ack_policy=AckPolicy.MANUAL)
async def bill(order: dict[str, int], msg: PubSubMessage, logger: Logger) -> None:
    try:
        # waits for the service to confirm the acknowledgement
        await msg.ack()
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("order %s was not confirmed", order["id"])
        raise

With the default policy the confirmation failure follows the usual path: the handler's message is nacked when the exception propagates.

docs.title: Graceful shutdown
docs.text:
On shutdown the subscriber stops reading, waits for the handlers in work up to the broker's graceful_timeout (15 seconds by default), sends the pending acks and returns the messages it still holds to the service, which delivers them to another consumer.

service.py
broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project", graceful_timeout=30.0)

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
PubSubTelemetryMiddleware traces and measures publishes and deliveries. Install the otel extra.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker
from faststream_gcp_pubsub.opentelemetry import PubSubTelemetryMiddleware

tracer_provider = TracerProvider()

broker = PubSubBroker(
    project_id="my-project",
    middlewares=(PubSubTelemetryMiddleware(tracer_provider=tracer_provider),),
)
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

The middleware takes tracer_provider, meter_provider, meter and include_messages_counters, as FastStream's TelemetryMiddleware does.

docs.title: Prometheus
docs.text:
PubSubPrometheusMiddleware exports the metrics of publishes and deliveries to a Prometheus registry. Install the prometheus extra.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream
from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry, make_asgi_app

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker
from faststream_gcp_pubsub.prometheus import PubSubPrometheusMiddleware

registry = CollectorRegistry()

broker = PubSubBroker(
    project_id="my-project",
    middlewares=(PubSubPrometheusMiddleware(registry=registry, app_name="billing"),),
)
app = FastStream(broker)

# serve the metrics: `app` mounted on any ASGI server, or `FastStream.as_asgi`
metrics_app = make_asgi_app(registry)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

The middleware takes registry, app_name, metrics_prefix, received_messages_size_buckets and custom_labels, as FastStream's PrometheusMiddleware does.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
publish sends one message and returns the message id the service assigned. publish_batch sends several messages in one request and returns their ids.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


async def place_orders() -> None:
    message_id = await broker.publish(
        {"id": 1},
        "orders",
        headers={"region": "eu"},
        ordering_key="customer-42",
        correlation_id="req-1",
    )
    ids = await broker.publish_batch({"id": 2}, {"id": 3}, topic="orders")
    assert isinstance(message_id, str)
    assert len(ids) == 2

A batch takes at most 1000 messages and 10 MB.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: Headers travel as message attributes. Values are strings on the wire, so another value type is sent as its str(). FastStream adds correlation_id, content-type and, when set, reply_to.

docs.title: Ordering keys
docs.text: Messages with one ordering key reach a subscription with enable_message_ordering=True in the order the service received them. Publish them one after another, awaiting each call: concurrent calls reach the service in any order.

docs.title: Message ids
docs.text: publish returns the id of the message and publish_batch returns a list of ids in the order of the messages. The consumer reads the id from msg.raw_message.message_id.

docs.title: Publisher objects
docs.text:
A publisher object keeps the topic and the defaults for every call.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


orders = broker.publisher(
    "orders",
    ordering_key="customer-42",
    headers={"source": "api"},
)


# a publisher object keeps its defaults for every call
async def place_order() -> None:
    await orders.publish({"id": 1})
    await orders.publish({"id": 2}, ordering_key="customer-43")

A call can replace the ordering key. Attributes given to a call are added to the publisher's.

Decorate a handler with a publisher to publish its return value, as the home page does with @shipments.

docs.title: Limits of the service
docs.text: The service rejects a message with too many or too long attributes, an ordering key above 1024 bytes, or a body above 10 MB. The error is the service's InvalidArgument. The test broker raises the same error.

docs.title: Replies
docs.text:
A message published with reply_to="<topic>" gets the handler's return value published to that topic.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("jobs-worker", topic="jobs")
async def run(job: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
    # published to the topic named by the message's `reply_to`
    return {"done": True, "job": job["id"]}


@broker.subscriber("results-client", topic="results")
async def collect(result: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


async def submit() -> None:
    await broker.publish({"id": 7}, "jobs", reply_to="results")

The reply is an ordinary message: the caller reads it from a subscription of the reply topic, as collect does.

docs.title: PubSubResponse
docs.text:
Return PubSubResponse to set the ordering key and the attributes (headers) of the reply. The same options apply to every publisher the handler is decorated with.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker, PubSubResponse

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("jobs-worker", topic="jobs")
async def run(job: dict[str, str]) -> PubSubResponse:
    return PubSubResponse(
        {"done": True},
        headers={"worker": "w1"},
        ordering_key=job["owner"],
    )


@broker.subscriber("results-client", topic="results")
async def collect(result: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

docs.title: No request/reply
docs.text: broker.request() raises FeatureNotSupportedException. Pub/Sub has no reply channel of its own: an answer to a request needs a reply subscription for each caller, and creating those is resource administration (a subscription and its permissions per caller). Publish with reply_to naming a topic your service subscribes to, and read the answer there.

docs.title: Routers
docs.text:
A router groups subscribers and publishers in a module and is included into the broker.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import (
    PubSubBroker,
    PubSubPublisher,
    PubSubRoute,
    PubSubRouter,
)

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)

router = PubSubRouter(prefix="billing-")


@router.subscriber("orders", topic="orders")
@router.publisher("receipts")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {"order_id": order["id"]}


async def notify(receipt: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


# routes declare handlers without a decorator
routes = PubSubRouter(
    prefix="shop-",
    handlers=(
        PubSubRoute(
            notify,
            "receipts",
            topic="receipts",
            publishers=(PubSubPublisher("notifications"),),
        ),
    ),
)

broker.include_router(router)
broker.include_router(routes)

PubSubRouter(prefix="billing-") prepends the prefix to the topic and subscription names it declares: the handler above reads billing-orders and publishes to billing-receipts.

docs.title: PubSubRoute and PubSubPublisher
docs.text: PubSubRoute registers a handler without a decorator: it takes the function, the subscription and the same options as @broker.subscriber. PubSubPublisher is a publisher registration that a route passes in publishers=. Routes go to the router's handlers=; routers nest with routers=.

docs.title: Options of the router
docs.text: PubSubRouter also accepts dependencies, middlewares, parser, decoder, ack_policy and include_in_schema. They apply to everything the router declares.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
TestPubSubBroker runs the broker in process, with no Pub/Sub service behind it.

test_service.py
@pytest.mark.asyncio()
async def test_bill_publishes_a_shipment() -> None:
    async with TestPubSubBroker(broker) as br:
        await br.publish({"id": 1}, "orders")

        bill.mock.assert_called_once_with({"id": 1})
        ship.mock.assert_called_once_with({"order_id": 1})

The service under test:

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSub, PubSubBroker, PubSubTopic

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="faststream-test")
app = FastStream(broker)

shipments = broker.publisher(PubSubTopic("shipments", declare=True))


@broker.subscriber(PubSub("orders-billing", declare=True), topic="orders")
@shipments
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {"order_id": order["id"]}


@broker.subscriber(PubSub("shipments-courier", declare=True), topic="shipments")
async def ship(shipment: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

A publish reaches the handlers directly. handler.mock records the decoded body of each call, and the handler's reply reaches the subscribers of its topic.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
The test broker routes the way the service does:

  • A topic delivers to every subscription attached to it.
  • The consumers of one subscription share its messages, in turn.
  • A subscription read by get_one() or iteration keeps what is published until it is read.
  • Ack, nack and reject settle the message once: each message reaches its handler one time.

A declaration always succeeds, and a publish reaches whichever subscriptions the service declares for its topic.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
A publish the service would reject raises the service's InvalidArgument: attribute names and sizes, the ordering key size, message and request size, and the resource id format.

test_service.py
@pytest.mark.asyncio()
async def test_a_rejected_publish_raises() -> None:
    async with TestPubSubBroker(broker) as br:
        with pytest.raises(InvalidArgument):
            await br.publish({"id": 1}, "orders", ordering_key="k" * 2000)

docs.title: Against the emulator
docs.text:
with_real=True runs the same test against a real service, such as the emulator. Declare the resources the service uses with declare=True, as the example service does.

test_service.py
@pytest.mark.gcp()
@pytest.mark.asyncio()
async def test_bill_with_the_emulator() -> None:
    async with TestPubSubBroker(broker, with_real=True) as br:
        await br.publish({"id": 1}, "orders")
        await bill.wait_call(10)

        bill.mock.assert_called_once_with({"id": 1})

Mark such tests gcp and run them with just test-gcp while the emulator is up.

docs.title: Topics and subscriptions
docs.text:
Pub/Sub keeps topics and subscriptions as separate resources. A publisher names a topic. A subscriber names a subscription attached to a topic.

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSubBroker

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber("orders-billing", topic="orders")
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


@broker.subscriber("orders-audit", topic="orders")
async def audit(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


# a subscription named without a topic is attached to the topic of the same name
@broker.subscriber("invoices")
async def archive(invoice: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...


# a full name is used as it is: this reads a subscription of another project
@broker.subscriber("projects/other-project/subscriptions/orders-export", topic="orders")
async def export(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

A message published to orders is delivered to both orders-billing and orders-audit. When several consumers read one subscription, they share its messages.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
A short id such as orders is expanded with the broker's project: projects/my-project/topics/orders. A name that starts with projects/ is a full name and is used as it is. This is how a subscriber reads a subscription of another project.

A subscription named without a topic is attached to the topic of the same name. The topic argument names what the subscription is attached to. The broker uses it to declare the resources, in the test broker routing and in the AsyncAPI document.

docs.title: Names as declarations
docs.text:
Both arguments also take a declaration, PubSub and PubSubTopic, which describes how to create the resource:

service.py
from faststream import FastStream

from faststream_gcp_pubsub import PubSub, PubSubBroker, PubSubTopic

broker = PubSubBroker(project_id="my-project")
app = FastStream(broker)


@broker.subscriber(
    PubSub("orders-billing", declare=True),
    topic=PubSubTopic("orders"),
)
async def bill(order: dict[str, int]) -> None: ...

See Declaring resources for every setting.
